evidence: The engine keys both relaxations on the flag alone: tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:225 never refuses a human author regardless of self_driving, review_pr.py:590 skips the draft prerequisite whenever self_driving is set, and review_local.py:321 sets the flag straight from context['self_driving_review']. The webhook re-review leg refutes the finding for every synchronize/reopen/retarget: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-172 returns an empty carve-out for any non-bot author before task linkage is consulted. The receiver leg does not: process_inbox_pr_review fetches the PR at tasks.py:1159 but stamps inbox_review at tasks.py:1176-1181 and :1229 with no author check, and activities.py:451 forwards that as the engine flag. A human-authored PR reaches it when a collaborator manually opens a PR from a self-driving run's pushed branch (bare-branch runs are a supported outcome), because the tasks webhook backstop at products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:159 and :184-185 binds any repo-native branch-matched PR into the run's output.pr_url with a fork check but no author check, which fires review_hog's receiver. The blast radius is small: the fork check guarantees the author has push access, the provenance block at reviewer.py:694-702 removes familiarity trust (stricter, not looser), and the outcome is a head-pinned approval on the collaborator's own draft that the normal path would grant after ready_for_review, with the LABEL-mode gate at tasks.py:944 as the only extra bypass. The engine-side coupling the finding asks for matches the 'bot-authored draft by construction' invariant the PR itself states and the webhook leg already enforces, so it is a cheap consistency fix rather than a must_fix.
notes: I would drop this to not_an_issue if TaskRun.branch for signals implementation runs does not hold the pushed head branch (breaking the backstop match) or if the agent server always opens the PR itself so bare-branch outcomes never occur; I would raise it to should_fix if approving a collaborator's draft without the LABEL-mode trigger label counts as a policy breach.
